items.text: Hey there College Football Fans, welcome back to the Campus Huddle, your source for all news and updates straight from the developers. It’s hard to believe we are in the middle of the College Football season already! We have a brand new Title Update releasing today, let's get into the details.
Added functionality to allow users to strafe while in Ballhawk.
Fixed an issue where the QB would super dive when attempting to slide near the first down line.
Fixed an issue where the Defensive Line would auto pinch or spread when audibling in or out of QB sneak.
Fixed an issue where Interceptions caught near and carried into the endzone would be ruled a Safety.

From the Devs: Hey there CFB 27 fans! Before we get started with what’s in this title update, from us to you we wanted to say thank you for your overwhelming response and feedback about the EA SPORTS Network! We have been reading all of it and are so happy that you are enjoying this passion project of ours to make you feel more immersed in your Dynasty. We will continue to read your feedback and make appropriate changes. Thank you!
Fixed an issue where the Top Story could not be viewed when the user team was playing in the National Championship.
Made several text based content updates throughout the EA SPORTS Network.
Fixed an issue where Coach Goals that awarded Dynasty Points would not correctly grant those points during the End of Season Recap.

Fixed an issue where Coach Points awarded after receiving a contract extension could be granted in values that were not multiples of five. Coach Point awards will now always be granted in multiples of five.
Updated the warning popup when firing a staff member to correctly account for the Dynasty Points refunded from firing the coach.
Fixed an issue where the Post-Game Stats screen could display a Please Wait message when attempting to view post-game stats.
Updated the Defensive Coordinator at North Carolina.
Fixed an issue where the William V. Campbell Trophy was missing its icon.
Fixed an issue in the Max Potential screen where some sliders could disappear after resetting all Max Potential allocations.
Fixed an issue where the game could freeze after selecting a Goal Line play during the Air Game minigame.
Fixed an issue where selecting Special Teams plays in certain scenarios as a non-quarterback could cause the game to freeze.

From the Devs: Hey Ultimate Team players! With TU5, we continued to improve Ultimate Captains, Objectives on Items, and EVOs, with a focus on clearer upgrade information and more reliable selection, filtering, and item-management flows.
Fixed an issue where the Buy Skill Points section appeared empty when viewing player Archetype upgrades.
Fixed an issue where the Max OVR shown during the New Ratings flow did not match the Max OVR displayed on the Upgrades screen.
Fixed an issue where Objectives on Items appeared locked in the Lineup until the user played a game.
Fixed issues where Objectives on Items did not display their favorited status consistently across Lineup tabs and could produce a server error when favorited from Special Teams.
Fixed an issue where an EVO could be applied to the first eligible player in the list instead of the player selected by the user.
Fixed a server error that could occur when opening filters in the EVO menu.
Fixed an issue where changing filters on the EVO player-selection screen could display blank or duplicated player items.
Fixed an issue where the EVO Upgrade Path preview did not display the rewards available from its objectives.
Fixed an issue where quickselling an item with a non-removable EVO could leave the item visible and lead to a server error.
Fixed an issue where the back of Ultimate Team player items did not display the player’s position or jersey number.
Fixed an issue where some in-game Ultimate Team player panels displayed jersey number 0.
Fixed an issue where the Field Pass Reward Path displayed the total XP threshold instead of the remaining XP needed to reach a level.
Fixed an issue where selecting Redeem on certain Sets returned an error even when at least one eligible item could be added.
Fixed an issue where Online Head-to-Head used the default uniforms instead of the uniforms selected in Advanced Settings.
Fixed an issue where some player item portraits were missing from the Ultimate Team H2H pregame presentation.

Hey there College Football Fans, welcome back to the Campus Huddle, your source for all news and updates straight from the developers! We hope you are enjoying last week's Roster Update! We have a lot to talk about with what's coming in tomorrow's Title Update so lets get right into it!

Dev Note: We’ve heard your feedback around Man Coverage and have been actively investigating. We want to be diligent with our approach to ensure Man Coverage remains a viable defensive strategy, but is balanced. Our team has reviewed player data and social sentiment. After further testing, we’ve identified targeted issues that could have contributed cases of overly effective man coverage. To address this, you will find the following fixes in today's update:
Pass Lead Tuning: Tuning to extend the default pass lead distance when throwing to a receiver running downfield.
Route Running: Fixed an issue where Elite Route Runners were not playing the appropriate cut animation on Zig routes.
WR/DB Jostle: Fixed an issue where Wide Receivers would not fully accelerate out of a jostle win.
WR/DB Jostle: Tuned Jostle animations so Receivers can keep better separation from lower rated DBs.
Man Press: Tuning to Man Press to increase the Penalty for shading in the wrong direction of the release.
Fixed an issue where Illegal Forward Pass was called when the QB was partially behind the line of scrimmage.
Fixed an issue where Combo Coverage would convert to Lock when in a press alignment.
Fixed an issue where Cloud Flats were ignoring user coaching adjustment drop depths and aggressively jumping short flat routes.
Fixed an issue where the User's Coverage Shell wasn't always respected coming out of playcall.
Fixed an issue that prevented users from calling defensive hot routes on players assigned to a man coverage check (like Combo).
Fixed an issue where calling Zone Drops through Custom Adjustments wouldn't update the play art on field.
Fixed an issue where receivers would start to drop the ball before a catch tackle knockout would play.
Added 'Perfect Hit vs Perfect Timing Knockout' text for Users on Defense when a knockout occurs after a Perfect Time Based Catch.

notes.title: Welcome to the EA SPORTS Network!

items.text: EA SPORTS Network is a brand new, dynamic storytelling system that turns your custom career path into an ongoing news hub. Instead of showing static one-off moments and basic statistics, you will now experience personalized news coverage, game previews, and post game recaps that change week over week based on your performance on the field. Here are some key notes for you to know about this new feature:

notes.title: Where can you experience the EA SPORTS Network

items.text: Road to Glory: You will experience this feature throughout your player's career journey.
Dynasty Mode: This feature will be experienced in either your offline or online Dynasty.

Authentic Storytelling: Your games are treated like real world news. The network dynamically reacts to major season moments, celebrating statement wins, breaking down tough rivalry losses, and highlighting standout player performances.

Increased Narrative Variety: You will now experience a more customized pool of Game Previews and Post Game Recaps. We did this so your weekly content can always feel fresh and unique to your schedule.

Updated News Tab: We Updated CFB News Tab to be the EA SPORTS Network in game so you know exactly where to go to experience this. Our goal here is to give you a deeper authentic experience that is easily accessible to you.
Dev Note: To access the full stories, Press Triangle/Y on your controller on a story within your Dynasty or Road To Glory hubs.

Dev Note: Hey there #CFB27 fans! We can’t wait for you to experience the EA Sports Network first hand tomorrow! Please let us know your thoughts and bring your feedback as we continue to improve this feature!

Hey there College Football Fans, welcome back to the Campus Huddle, your source for all news and updates straight from the developers! We have a lot to cover today to get you geared up for tomorrow's title update which includes Gameplay Updates, New Uniforms, and more! Let's get started!
Slightly lowered the frequency of pancake blocks occurring during gameplay.
Made coaching adjustment changes designed to better address situations where pancake blocks were triggering more often than intended.
Tuned aggressive blocking and defender aggression interactions to help improve the balance of pancake block outcomes.

Dev Note: We’ve seen your feedback around pancake blocks happening more often than expected in certain gameplay situations. This update takes a two-pronged approach by slightly lowering pancake block frequency while also making coaching adjustment changes to better address the root of the issue. We will continue to monitor feedback after this update goes live.
Improved blocking logic for targeting and assignment execution.
Improved receiver vs. defensive back block outcomes so dominant wins occur at a more balanced rate and feel more situational.
Improved backfield blocker behavior on chip-and-release assignments.
Fixed an issue where chip-and-release blockers could take poor initial angles.
Improved pass blocker depth on quick pass protection.
Fixed an issue where certain tackle over adjustments could create unrealistic interior rush lanes.
Improved play action pass protection so blockers drop back to a more appropriate depth.
Improved stunt logic and functionality.
Fixed multiple issues where Pirate Stunts could cause pass protection to leave rushers unblocked.
Improved defensive tackle loop behavior on stunts to reduce collisions and spacing issues.
Improved Jump the Snap timing feedback so it better matches the actual timing window.
Added Player Lock UI feedback for successful pass rush timing.
Adjusted the Jump the Snap timing window to improve pass rush feel.
Improved defender ability to shed blocks in the proper run-fit direction.
Improved run block double-team shed triggers for defenders.
Improved defender behavior on jump balls and interception attempts to allow for higher catch points.
Improved catch tackle interactions and knockout chances in Contested Scenarios.
Fixed an issue where defenders could fail to trigger a catch tackle during catch interactions.
Fixed an issue where catch holes could occur on accurately thrown high-point bullet passes.
Fixed an issue where defenders in hit reactions could incorrectly transition into chase-ball behavior during catch interactions.
Improved Cover 3 Match Checks logic vs 4 strong where the weakside seam flat will play with better tempo and not get as much width.
Fixed an issue where an Outside Third defender in Cover 3 Blitz could incorrectly match a return route instead of dropping into the intended Outside Third assignment.
Fixed an issue in Cover 3 Match Skinny Checks where the #3 receivers could be left open on a corner route in Gun Trips TE when the tight end was on a drag route.
Fixed an issue where the Safety would slow down in Buzz Coverage and 3 High Structure Defenses
Updated Bracket/Double Team logic and leverage to allow the deep defender to take better angles.
Fixed an issue in Cover 3 Match where hook/curl defenders would still play skate rules runs vs bunch after Underneath or Over The Tops coverage adjustments were made.
Improved Stubbie and Stump push logic in Cover 4 Palms against backside running back swing routes to create 4 strong..
Added logic for cornerbacks in press alignment to play M.E.G. in Cover 4 Quarters.
Bingo and Box Check Logic Improvements for the CB and Quarter Flats Pattern Recognition.
Increased CPU coaching variety using different coverage checks and plaster settings.

Dev Note: More aggressive coaches may now favor aggressive checks and tighter plaster behavior, while conservative coaches will emphasize safer adjustments, we expect this to result in greater strategic variety and authenticity against teams.
Fixed an issue where Untarget Defender was not working correctly when showing blitz.
The Untarget User Defender coaching adjustments will no longer work on run plays. You will however be able to use the target defender on run plays at the line of scrimmage.
Fixed an issue where Untarget User Defender could apply while controlling a defensive lineman.
Fixed an issue where users had no way to scroll by subsection when creating a Custom Adjustment.
Dev Note: Pressing LT/RT will now allow players to scroll by section when creating custom adjustments.
Fixed an issue where CPU zone strategy changes could be revealed to the offense after an audible.
Improved the defender aggression coaching adjustment for run fit behavior vs Play Action.

Dev Note: Aggressive settings cause second level defenders to trigger downhill faster against the run, creating larger windows behind them. Conservative settings keep defenders more disciplined, allowing them to stay underneath intermediate routes and react more effectively to play action.
Fixed a Formation Shift issue where personnel could be manipulated to get 4 or 5 receivers into heavy sets.
Fixed an issue where the first team in the third overtime series could be placed at the 33-yard line instead of the 3-yard line.
Fixed an issue where the Dive Tutorial would not register dive actions and could not be completed.
Fixed an issue where players could freeze in place after certain get-up animations.
Fixed various post play issues with get up’s and frozen players.
Fixed an issue where a safety could get stuck during Nickel 2-4 Single Mug DB Blitz Tex 3.
Fixed an Issue in Online Play-A-Friend which caused unintended Stiff Arm behavior.
Added new Cover 4 Zone, Cover 6 Zone, and Cover 9 Zone plays to select defensive playbooks.
Dev Note: These plays serve as preset coverages that do not match and play vision/break “Zone it” rules vs all formations. Just like Cover 4 drop, the safeties are not in run fits for these plays.
Added 12 new Press Quarters plays to the Press Quarters playbook.
Added three new blitzes to the 3-3-5 Odd Ghost Playbook to give the formation additional support for pressure.
Added 4-3 Under Wide to the 4-2-5 Zone Pressure playbook, giving the playbook at least one base defense option.

Speed Boosting.
Instances of slot DB's not flipping when they should.
Man Coverage Effectiveness.

Multiple stability fixes.

We’ve loved seeing the creativity and attention to detail the community has brought to life with Team Builder, and we want to ensure the experience remains reliable for both Team Builder creators and players who download teams.
We’re aware of an issue impacting some players’ ability to update Team Builder teams between Dynasty seasons.

After investigation, we identified unsupported Team Builder assets and teams exceeding the supported uniform limit as factors that can prevent created teams from updating correctly and affect players who download them.

Team Builder is designed around specific asset and uniform limits to support reliable performance across the web experience and in-game. Teams that exceed those limits can require additional memory and processing, which may contribute to slower performance, failed updates, and stability issues for creators and players who download them.

We’re currently testing a fix to improve Team Builder and Dynasty stability. Once released, unsupported fonts and textures may be removed from affected teams, and up to five uniform combinations will be available in-game.
Created teams will remain available. For teams with more than five uniform combinations, we recommend placing the five uniforms you want to keep in the first five uniform slots ahead of the update.
Stay tuned to @CFBDirect to know when this issue is resolved.

Dev Note: This update is in response to a small segment of players exploiting single game achievements.

Fixed an issue where During quizzes, you would not see what the correct answer was after selecting an answer.

Introducing EVOs, a new progression system that gives you more control over how your roster develops throughout the year. Whether you're investing in a player you've believed in since day one or finding new ways to strengthen your lineup, EVOs let you shape your team your way.

These non-player items will give you more flexibility in how you upgrade your lineup, add new paths to improve your favorite players, and create more reasons to keep building around the players you want on the field. You will not be able to swap out player items after you select who to give an EVO to, so choose wisely.

EVOs will live in their own dedicated menu tile, including free EVOs, EVOs earned through objectives, and purchasable EVOs. These will cycle in and out as we drop more programs. Check back often to see what is available and what upgrades can help take your team to the next level!
At any given time, all players will have access to at least one free EVO: the Program Pillar EVO.
Starting on August 8th, you can find the Program Pillar EVO on the first page of the EVO Store.

The Program Pillar EVO can be applied to any Core player item, regardless of position or archetype, and adds a dynamic upgrade path that lets you increase that player’s OVR over time. The OVR cap for your Program Pillar will continue to increase throughout the year, giving you a long-term upgrade path as new content rolls out.

Once a player is placed into the Program Pillar EVO, you’ll unlock objectives that can be completed by playing with that player item in your lineup. Completing those objectives earns SP, which is used to increase that player’s OVR.
Additional limited-time free EVOs will also arrive with select programs throughout the year.
Supercharge your biggest playmakers.

Launching alongside the SUPERCHARGED program on August 7th, these program specific EVOs are designed to take your Super Charged player items even further. Increase OVR upgrade caps, unlock powerful new abilities, and open exclusive upgrade paths tied directly to the program.
Some Supercharged EVOs can even be applied to Core player items, giving you even more flexibility to build creative lineups and bring your favorite players into your long-term plans.

We believe that no two EVOs should look the same! Arriving on August 7th, Core EVOs provide even more ways to personalize your roster and will refresh regularly in the EVO Store throughout the year and will continue to refresh frequently in the EVO Store throughout the year.
These EVOs are not tied to the Supercharged program and are designed to offer more ways to customize and upgrade your team. Here are a few examples of Core EVOs you may see:
Max OVR EVOs: Raise the max OVR on an upgradable player.
Archetype EVOs: Add or change position archetype upgrade paths.
Chemistry EVOs: Add or change team or scheme chemistries.
Ability EVOs: Add or change abilities on your player item.
We will continue releasing new EVOs and updating existing EVOs throughout the year, giving you more ways to shape your lineup, boost your player items, and build your team your way.

Hey College Football fans, welcome to the Campus Huddle!
Last week, we shared that paid progression options were being removed from Road to Glory and Online Dynasty in College Football 27 and they are officially out as of July 11th.

Today’s Campus Huddle follows up that message and shares how progression is designed in College Football 27, how Dynasty Blueprint and Road to Glory are tuned, more information on Road to Glory progression and what’s coming in our Title Update this week.
Dynasty Blueprint is the core difference between College Football 26 and College Football 27.

Coming out of College Football 26, one of the clearest pieces of feedback was that rebuilds could become too easy, too quickly. Dynasty Blueprint was built to create a deeper, more challenging simulation where long term building and sustaining a program requires more than stacking wins.
That means coach progression had to support the full Blueprint experience.

Coach Level is not a legacy score. It is not a direct reflection of wins and losses. Coach Levels give you Coach Points, and Coach Points are how you choose which skill trees and perks to focus on throughout your career.

In College Football 25, the max coach level was 50. Many players reached that cap early in their career arc, which left them with no additional levels to work towards and no additional Coach Points to earn. In College Football 26, we expanded the cap to 100 based on that feedback. Level 75 became roughly equivalent to a maxed College Football 25 coach in terms of abilities owned, with 25 additional levels added as endgame progression.

That structure continues in College Football 27. The goal is not for every coach to quickly reach level 100. The goal is to give players more years of meaningful Coach Point decisions across a 20–30 year career.

The fastest way to advance your coach is to lean into your active Coach Archetype perk and advance into higher-tier archetypes. Each archetype tier rewards more XP, so moving from base archetypes into Elite, Hybrid, Program Builder, and CEO paths can significantly accelerate your growth. Your staff matters too: you share in XP earned when other coaches on your staff trigger their active archetype perk, making coordinator hires and staff strengths a key part of coach progression.

Your accomplishments on the field still matter. Winning games, meeting goals, and performing at a high level all contribute to progression. But coach progression is about demonstrating mastery through the systems that define your coach: archetype, staff, skill trees, program building decisions, and long term results. Some abilities can also increase XP gains or reduce ability costs based on your staff, making those decisions another part of your long term progression strategy.

College Football 27 also has annual contract payouts as another way to earn Coach Points. These payouts scale based on your coach level, prestige, success, and the size of your school. Contract extensions from your current school can increase that payout, creating another meaningful Coaching Carousel decision.
Even at level 100, you cannot unlock every perk, an intentional choice as no coach can be great at everything, and every decision should matter.

Dynasty Blueprint is built around that idea. Your coach, your staff, your school resources, your recruiting strategy, your AD expectations, your program goals, and your long-term decisions all work together. There is no single solved path to building a great program.
While that long term arc remains important to the design of Dynasty, we want to reiterate the immediate changes coming to Dynasty.
In the next Title Update, we are updating our Coach XP Speed Settings based on feedback. Going forward we will replace the current sliders with 3 new setting options.

notes.title: The three new Coach XP Speed Settings are

items.text: Career: Authentic long term coach progression at 1.0x XP. This is equivalent to the previous College Football 27 default setting and is best for players who want the full Dynasty Blueprint experience, where every Coach Point and coaching decision carries more weight across the life of a Dynasty.

The Career setting is the new default Coach XP Speed setting and the intended Dynasty Blueprint experience. This is our design vision and truly captures how difficult it can be to build and sustain a successful program. The feedback we have heard is that it should be more challenging to rebuild smaller schools and now it is.
Simulation: Balanced coach progression at 1.25x XP. This is best for players who want a realistic pace while still progressing their coach at a faster rate.

Casual: Fastest coach progression at 1.5x XP. This is equivalent to the Faster setting from College Football 26 and is best for players who want to unlock abilities quickly and accelerate coach growth.

Note: These new settings will take effect in existing Dynasties. Coach XP Speed Settings will be available in both Online and Offline Dynasty. In Online Dynasty, league commissioners will control the Coach XP Speed Setting for the entire league.
As we looked at player feedback, our goal was to provide more flexibility in coach progression without compromising the long-term progression that Dynasty Blueprint is designed to deliver.

Coach XP Speed Settings apply to every coach in Dynasty, including CPU coaches. When progression moves too quickly, too many coaches reach high-end abilities too early, elite programs separate even faster, and the systems that define Dynasty Blueprint start to matter less: coach archetypes, staff building, recruiting, AD expectations, school resources, Coach Points, and long-term program goals.
That is why “Fastest” is not returning. The new Coach XP Speed Settings are designed to give players more control over progression pace while preserving the long term balance of Dynasty Blueprint.

notes.title: Road to Glory Progression and XP Sliders

items.text: Standalone XP sliders are not returning to Road to Glory because progression in College Football 27 is now built around the full structure of the mode: difficulty, weekly decisions, Fitness, NIL deals, Wear and Tear, Legacy Score, scholarship bonuses, and on-field performance.

The Weekly Agenda is tuned around the full player management loop in College Football 27. Fitness and Leadership both impact how quickly you earn progression XP, giving players more control over growth across the season. Keeping those meters high can accelerate progression, while letting them drop can slow it down. Road to Glory also places more weight on difficulty, rewarding players who take on the greater challenge. Wear and Tear is another core part of that balance. When Wear and Tear is turned off, one of the mode’s progression challenges is removed, so the XP modifier adjusts with it.

Difficulty is also a progression lever. Throwing for 500 yards on Freshman and throwing for 500 yards on Heisman are different accomplishments, and College Football 27 rewards those accomplishments differently. Higher difficulty creates higher progression opportunities because the challenge is greater, but players can still reach max rating on Freshman over the course of their career.

We’ve also seen feedback that Road to Glory players can start at a lower OVR than they did in College Football 26. That is intentional and tied to how progression is now paced across the full career. College Football 27 adds annual scholarship bonuses to create more offseason progression, with bonuses paying out each year instead of progression being concentrated only at the start of your career or week to week. Playing through High School also matters, because skipping High School means skipping that first year progression modifier. Your starting point may look different, but this does not lower what your player can ultimately become.
Road to Glory also uses OVR ceilings tied to Legacy Score. Increasing your Legacy Score by proving yourself on the field is part of raising your player’s long term ceiling.

We will continue to evaluate Road to Glory progression over time and make tuning adjustments where needed. The core structure, however, is intentional and is the foundation of Road to Glory moving forward.
